subject: Quick follow-up from Inference Lab — next steps & short recap
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from Inference Lab — next steps & short recap

Hi Sophie — great to meet you at the Inference Lab panel last week. Thanks again for the quick hallway chat about CloudInfra's real-time inference needs. I promised a short recap and a proposed next step.

Recap (from our conversation):
- Current pain: unpredictable tail latency for multi-tenant feature-service workflows during batch windows.
- Workload: mixed chat + structured completion calls, average seq len ~400 tokens, 200–400 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Priority: Q4 cost and latency reduction is a 2 on a 1–3 scale; security and auditability are blockers for any managed offering.

What Redwood can help with (suggested):
- Dedicated pool with autoscale-burst for predictable throughput.
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce token spend on repeated context.
- Route cold fallbacks to a quantized variant to preserve SLA when capacity is constrained.

Proposed next step:
1) 30-minute discovery call next week to walk through a short profiling checklist (we'll ask for a small set of representative traces + a quick README of model variants).
2) We'll run a 2-week proof-of-value on dedicated capacity with cost/latency baselines and SLOs.

I attached a short demo deck and a sample MAP (mutual action plan) template to guide scope. Can you share availability for a 30-min slot? Tuesday/Wednesday morning PT are open on our side.

Thanks — Vivek

--

- Procurement: procurement asks for a simple SOW and estimated cost band before committing to reserved capacity.
